neighbours.label: The word that closes an elliptical clause standing in for an earlier verb phrase ('to do so', 'if they do,', 'or else'), vs the same sentences with the verb phrase spelled out
fire: He planned to sell the house, but he never found the courage to do so.
Few birds stay here in winter, and if they do, they hide in the reeds.
You must finish the form by noon, or else the office will reject it.
Some of the guests might want to leave early; if they do, call a taxi.
She was asked to resign but refused to do so until the inquiry ended.
Keep the dog on a lead, or else it will chase the sheep again.
Most patients do not feel pain, and if they do, it fades within hours.
The team was free to change the design, but chose not to do so in the end.
quiet: He planned to sell the house, but he never found a buyer for the place.
Few birds stay here in winter, and the ones that stay hide in the reeds.
You must finish the form by noon, because the office closes at one.
Some of the guests might want to leave early; please call them a taxi.
She was asked to resign but stayed in her post until the inquiry ended.
Keep the dog on a lead near the field where the sheep are grazing.
Most patients do not feel pain, and the mild ache fades within hours.
The team was free to change the design, but kept the original plan in the end.
